title: Tenant Eviction Simulator & Operator Playbook
author: Marcus Leung
body:
Summary
-------
This document describes the Tenant Eviction Simulator (TES) service, operational runbooks for controlled tenant eviction events, and the associated dashboards and alerting needed to safely reclaim capacity under cost or safety pressure. TES is an operator-facing tool used during sustained capacity constraints, multi-tenant overload, or when a soft quota policy must be enforced to protect SLOs for higher-priority customers.

Goals
-----
- Provide a deterministic, observable simulation of eviction policies before applying them in production.
- Minimize user-facing errors and tail-latency impact during tenant eviction or soft-throttling events.
- Give operators clear decision steps, rollback criteria, and automated safety checks.

Scope
-----
- Applies to Redwood Dedicated and Hosted multi-tenant pools managed by the scheduler service (traffic-shepherd + tenant-priority-rebalancer).
- Does NOT control on-prem private deployments (those follow Private Ops playbooks).
- Eviction actions include: soft quota (rate-limit), background eviction (batching) and hard preemption (GPU reclamation).

Key definitions
---------------
- Soft quota: temporary per-tenant token-rate cap that gracefully reduces throughput.
- Background eviction: reclaiming low-priority allocated work items (queued batches) with minimal interruption.
- Hard preemption: killing running instances/tasks for immediate capacity; highest-impact and last resort.
- Candidate tenant: tenant selected by policy for eviction actions.

Service architecture (high level)
--------------------------------
Components involved:
- traffic-shepherd: gateway that applies per-tenant hints and priority tokens.
- tenant-priority-rebalancer: periodic decision engine that ranks tenants by SLA, spend, and heuristics.
- kv-prefix-cache: LRU-backed prefix cache that can be persisted during eviction planning.
- scheduler: orchestrates pod eviction and node-level rebalancing.
- tes-simulator: the new simulation service that replays telemetry and predicts SLO impact.

TES inputs and outputs
---------------------
Inputs (examples):
- Recent 1h/6h/24h token rate by tenant (prometheus:redwood_tokens_by_tenant_total)
- P50/P95/P99 latency slices by tenant and route (prometheus histogram).
- Active model counts, average kv cache hit rate, and per-tenant batch sizes.
- Tenant priority metadata: tier (gold, silver, bronze), contract SLA, and reserved capacity.

Outputs:
- Risk score (0-100) for each eviction policy per tenant.
- Predicted SLO delta for top-5 affected routes.
- Recommended action (no-op | soft-quota | background-evict | hard-preempt) with confidence bands.
- Synthetic trace samples and example error rates to inject into staging dashboards.

Operational runbook: staging first
--------------------------------
1) Prepare staging replay:
   - Start a replay job that uses the last 24h of telemetry: raptorctl replay start --window 24h --tenants <candidate-list> --out tes-job-<id>
   - Confirm KV cache seeding is enabled: kubectl -n runtime set env deployment/kv-seeder ENABLE_SEED=true
2) Run simulator in dry-run mode:
   - curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' https://tes.internal/api/v1/simulate -d '{"job":"tes-job-<id>","policies":["soft-quota","background-evict","hard-preempt"]}'
   - Expect JSON report; save to /var/lib/tessim/reports/timestramp.json for audit.
3) Validate dashboards:
   - Open staging dashboard: Grafana -> Platform -> TES Simulation / tes-job-<id>
   - Run the "Simulated SLO Delta" panel and confirm P95 latency change < 10% for gold tenants in dry-run.
4) Peer-review and sign-off (Reviewer must be SRE on-call + Platform PM).

Production runbook: safe rollout
------------------------------
Prerequisites:
- Active on-call SRE and an operator in the deployment window.
- Current cluster capacity >= 8% headroom OR approval from capacity manager.
- Incident channel created: #ops-tenant-eviction-<id>.

Steps:
1) Run TES for last 6h to generate final risk scores.
   - Endpoint: POST https://tes.internal/api/v1/simulate-live with body {"window":"6h","candidates": [...]} 
2) Apply soft-quota to low-risk tenants first:
   - traffic-shepherd supports a runtime API: POST /admin/tenant-quota/{tenant_id} {"tokens_per_minute": <value>, "expires_at": "2026-03-02T15:30:00Z"}
   - Monitor: promql: sum(rate(redwood_tokens_by_tenant_total[5m])) by (tenant)
3) Monitor safety gates for 30 minutes. Abort if any of the following triggers:
   - Gold-tenant P95 latency increases > 15% vs baseline.
   - Error budget burn for any tiered SLA > 5% in 30m window.
   - New sustained P99 spikes lasting > 5m for priority routes.
4) If soft-quota insufficient, schedule background-eviction for specific queues:
   - scheduler API: POST /v1/evict/background with {"tenant_ids": [...], "max_inflight_reclaim": 20}
   - Ensure kv-prefix-cache persists most-recent prefixes: rollout kv-seeder policy to keep top-10 prefixes pinned.
5) Hard preemption only with executive approval and cross-team notification. Follow emergency-model-swap runbook.

Rollback criteria and actions
----------------------------
- Immediate rollback if any gold tenant error-rate increases > 2x baseline. Action: remove all TES-applied quotas and trigger full warmup of evicted work (raptorctl warmup start --tag <evicted-job-id>).
- If operator sees tail-latency drift: run quick-restore: POST traffic-shepherd /admin/restore-tenant/{tenant_id}

Dashboards and alerts mapping
----------------------------
Essential dashboards (names and panels):
- Platform / TES / Live Simulation Overview
  - Panel: Risk score by policy (table)
  - Panel: Predicted P95 delta per route (heatmap)
- Platform / Tenant Health / Eviction Window
  - Panel: Per-tenant token rate, cpu/gpu usage, kv cache hit rate
- Platform / SLO Guardrails
  - Panel: Tiered error budget burn, P95 and P99 by tier

Example PromQL alerts to create (start with conservative thresholds):
- name: GoldTenantLatencySpike
  expr: (avg_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,route,tenant))[10m:5m]) > 1.15 * kube_service:baseline_p95{tier=\"gold\"})
  for: 5m
  labels: severity=page
  annotations: summary=\"Gold tenant P95 >15% above baseline\"

- name: EvictionRiskHigh
  expr: tes_risk_score{policy=\"hard-preempt\"} > 80
  for: 1m
  labels: severity=alert
  annotations: summary=\"High predicted impact for hard preempt on tenant {{ $labels.tenant }}\"

Operator CLI snippets
---------------------
- Start a safe dry-run simulation:
  raptorctl jobs create --type tes --window 6h --tenants tenant-a,tenant-b --mode dry-run
- Apply a soft quota (example):
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    https://traffic-shepherd.internal/admin/tenant-quota/tenant-b \
    -d '{"tokens_per_minute": 1200, "reason": "eviction-sim-test-2026-03-02"}'
- Revoke a quota:
  curl -X DELETE -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' https://traffic-shepherd.internal/admin/tenant-quota/tenant-b

Safety checklist (pre-apply)
---------------------------
- [ ] On-call SRE + operator assigned and paged.
- [ ] Staging simulation matched production replay for last 24h with <5% prediction error.
- [ ] KV cache seed validated and pinned prefixes identified.
- [ ] Communication channel established and customers in scope notified per policy.

Post-action retrospective template
--------------------------------
Include these items in the runbook retrospective within 72 hours:
1) Event summary and timeline (minutes precision).
2) Top-5 impacted routes and observed vs predicted deltas.
3) Operator actions and decision points (who approved hard actions).
4) Root cause if evictions required (capacity drift, hot workload, misconfiguration).
5) Action items and owners; expected completion dates.

Known limitations and risk mitigations
------------------------------------
- TES does not perfectly model cross-tenant KV cache interference when new model versions are loaded. Mitigation: conservative confidence bands and additional warmup windows.
- Hard preemption predictions have high variance for bursty customers. Mitigation: require 2x cross-validation runs and manual approval.

Roadmap items (Q2–Q4 2026)
--------------------------
- Q2: Add per-route gradient-descent optimizer to recommend soft-quota values that minimize SLO delta.
- Q3: Integrate TES with console rollouts for one-click staging->prod application with approval gating.
- Q4: Add automated rollback playbooks that use live traffic canaries to validate applied evictions.

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Primary owner: Platform SRE (team: eng-platform-sre).
- Service author: Marcus Leung (Platform runtime).
- Escalation: On-call SRE (see /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/operator-oncall-roster-2026).

Related reading
---------------
- Tenant isolation economics playbook (for pricing and tiered behavior).
- Emergency model swap and token surge mitigation runbook (hard preemption link).

Appendix A: Example simulation report (truncated)
------------------------------------------------
| tenant | recommended_action | risk_score | predicted_p95_delta | notes |
|--------|--------------------|------------|---------------------|-------|
| tenant-b | soft-quota | 28 | +3% | safe to apply for 30m window |
| tenant-x | background-evict | 62 | +11% | recommend eviction of queued jobs only |
| tenant-z | hard-preempt | 89 | +45% | exec approval required; high variance |

Appendix B: Audit trail requirements
-----------------------------------
- All TES actions must be logged to audit-log service with fields: operator_id, action, affected_tenants, decision_report_id, timestamp.
- Retain auditable artifacts for 365 days for enterprise customers.
